tb-205-2.question:
A nail is being removed from a piece of wood by a hammer (Fig b). When a force of 100 N is applied perpendicularly at the end of the handle of the hammer, the hammer is just able to turn about O and remove the nail. What is the friction f exerted on the nail by the wood? Assume that the hammer exerts a force parallel to f on the nail and the weight of the nail is negligible.

A 1.5 N

B 30 N

C 35 N

D 600 N
tb-205-2.reasoning:
Take moment about O.

Clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment

100 × 0.3 = f × 0.05

f = 600 N

tb-205-3.question:
A dog of weight 90 N remains at rest on a horizontal ground (Fig c). It is supported by the ground at points X and Y. The horizontal distances of its c.g. from X and Y are 15 cm and d respectively. The normal force acting on its front legs by the ground at X is 70 N. Find d.

A 11.7 cm

B 15 cm

C 20 cm

D 52.5 cm
tb-205-3.reasoning:
Take moment about Y.

Clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment

70 × (15 + d) = 90 × d

d = 52.5 cm

tb-205-4.question:
Two workers M and N carry a long iron bar on their shoulders (Fig d). M is closer to the c.g. of the iron bar than N.

If the forces they act on the iron bar point vertically upwards, who provides a larger force?

A M

B N

C They provide forces with the same magnitude.

D Cannot be determined
tb-205-4.reasoning:
Take moment about the c.g. of the iron bar.

The moments of the forces exerted on the bar by the two workers must cancel each other.

By τ = Fd, as M is closer to the c.g. of the iron bar than N, the force exerted by M on the iron bar is larger than that by M.

D 72 N
tb-205-5.reasoning:

F × 1.25 = 150 × 0.1

F = 12 N

tb-205-7.question:

If the object is in equilibrium, which arrow best represents the third force?

B Q

tb-205-7.reasoning:

tb-205-8.question:
Two identical rods P and Q lean against a smooth wall at different angles (Fig h). They remain at rest. FP and FQ are respectively the normal force acting on P and Q by the wall.

Which of the following is correct?

A FP > FQ

B FP = FQ

C FP < FQ

D The relationship between FP and FQ cannot be determined.
tb-205-8.reasoning:
Let θ be the angle between the rod and the ground.

Let l be the length of the rod.

Take moment about the lower end of the rod.

Clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment

Fl sin θ = W(l2)cos θ

F =W2tanθ

∴ F decreases as θ increases (for 0° < θ < 90°).

tb-205-9.question:
(For Q9−10). A uniform gangplank of weight 200 N is hinged smoothly to a ferry at point O. It is held stationary by a string attached to its c.g. (Fig i).

What is the tension in the string?

A 100 N

B 153 N

C 200 N

D 245 N
tb-205-9.reasoning:
Let d be the distance of the c.g. of the gangplank from O.

Take moment about O.

Clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment

Wd cos (180° – 160°) = Td sin 50°

200 cos 20° = T sin 50°

T = 245 N

tb-205-10.question:
(For Q9−10). A uniform gangplank of weight 200 N is hinged smoothly to a ferry at point O. It is held stationary by a string attached to its c.g. (Fig i).

In which direction does the force acting on the gangplank by the ferry at O point (Fig j)?

A P

B Q

C R

D SFig jS
tb-205-10.reasoning:
Take moment about the c.g. of the gangplank.

The moment of the force acting on the gangplank by the ferry should be zero.

∴ P and R are incorrect.

The net force acting on the gangplank is zero.

∴ S is incorrect.

tb-205-11.question:
Sam of weight 500 N stands on a diving board which is fixed by two supports at points X and Y as shown (Fig k). The weight of the board is 200 N and the c.g. of the board is 1.2 m from Y.

Sam walks from the position shown in Figure k to Y. Which of the following best describes the change in the force acting on the board by the support at X?

A Decreases in magnitude and remains upwards

B Decreases in magnitude and remains downwards

C Decreases in magnitude and eventually changes from upwards to downwards

D Increases in magnitude and remains downwards
tb-205-11.reasoning:
Take moment about Y.

Moment by the weight of the board

= 200 × 1.2 = 240 N m (clockwise)

When Sam is at the initial position,

moment by Sam’s weight

= 500 × 0.6 = 300 N m (anticlockwise)

Therefore, the force by X is pointing upwards (clockwise moment) so that the net moment is zero.

When Sam walks to Y, the moment by Sam decreases to zero. The force by X decreases and eventually changes its direction and points downwards (anticlockwise moment).

tb-205-12.question:
A pot holder is hung on a vertical fence (Fig l). P and Q are the two contact points between the holder and the fence. The force acting on the holder at Q by the fence is along the horizontal direction. The common c.g. of the pot and the holder is at C. Which arrow best shows the direction of the force acting on the holder at P by the fence?

A WX

B XZ

C Y

D Z
tb-205-12.reasoning:
Take moment about P.

The net moment is zero. The moment of the weight is anticlockwise. Therefore, the moment of the force at Q is clockwise. The force is pointing to the left.

Take moment about C.

The moment of the force at Q is clockwise. Therefore, the moment of the force at P is anticlockwise.

∴ Y and Z are incorrect.

The net force acting on the holder is zero. The horizontal component of the force at P should point to the right.

∴ W is incorrect.

tb-205-13.question:
A man is practicing human flag in a park (Fig m). He holds points P and Q on a vertical ladder. These two points are 1 m apart. His weight is 700 N and his c.g. is 0.8 m from the ladder.

What is the horizontal component of the force acting on him at Q by the ladder?

A 280 N (towards left)

B 280 N (towards right)

C 560 N (towards left)

D 560 N (towards right)
tb-205-13.reasoning:
Take moment about P.

Let FX be the horizontal component of the force acting on the man at Q.

Clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment

FX × 1 = 700 × 0.8

FX = 560 N

The horizontal component of the force acting on the man at Q is 560 N (towards left).

tb-205-14.question:
A plank PQ leans against a smooth wall (Fig n).

How do the normal force N and friction f acting on the plank at Q change when a cat walks at a constant velocity from Q to P? The plank remains at rest.

Option

N

f

increases

increases

increases

decreases

remains unchanged

remains unchanged

tb-205-14.reasoning:
The net force acting on the plank is zero.

Consider the vertical direction. The weights of the cat and the plank are unchanged.

tb-205-24.question:
Read the following passage about pet’s bowls and answer the questions that follow.

Pet owners usually use special bowls to hold their pets’ food (Fig ab).

This kind of bowl has a low centre of gravity and a large base radius compared with its height. Besides, the side of the bowl is not vertical, but slanted. These features reduce the chance of it toppling. We shall see below that increasing the base radius alone can help stabilize the bowl.

Let P be the centre of gravity of the bowl, Q be the point on the ground vertically below P and W be the weight of the bowl. Suppose a force F is exerted on the bowl so that the bowl tends to topple clockwise about T (Fig ac). Consider the moment τ of W about T:

τ = W × QT

This moment is anticlockwise and therefore tends to balance the moment by F. It can be seen that increasing QT (i.e. the base radius) helps stabilize the bowl.

(a) A dog licks point S of its bowl after a meal (Fig ad). It exerts a force of 3 N up the slanted surface. The base radius of the bowl is 9 cm. The slanted surface makes an angle of 45° to the ground. The bowl is 5 cm high.

(i) Find the moment of the 3-N force about T. (2 marks)

(ii) Show that in this case, decreasing the slanting angle helps stabilize the bowl. (2 marks)

(b) The dog accidentally kicks point S with a horizontal force 10 N. Find the moment of this force about T. (1 mark)
tb-205-24.answer:
(a) (i) Moment about T

= 3 × (0.09 × 2) × sin 45° 1M

= 0.382 N m (clockwise) 1A

(ii) By decreasing the slanting angle, the moment of the force by the dog about T decreases. 1A

The bowl becomes less likely to topple. 1A

(b) Zero 1A
